translations.attributionText: Rowwad Translation Center, provided by QuranEnc. Translation and footnotes are unmodified.
translations.footnotes: [3] This passage refers to the land of the three great prophets of Allah: Jesus (ﷺ) lived in the land of figs and olives, Moses (ﷺ) communicated with Allah on Mount Sinai, and Muhammad's (ﷺ) birthplace was Makkah. There is a similar reference in Deuteronomy 33:1, [Moses said:] “The Lord came from Sinai. Rising from Seir upon us, and he shone forth from Mount Paran.” Seir is a mountain near Jerusalem, and Paran is a mountain near Makkah.
translations.text: and by this secure city [of Makkah][3],
translations.transcriptInfo: Translated by the team of the Rowwad Translation Center, in cooperation with the Rabwah Dawah Association, the Islamic Content Service Association in Languages, and the IslamHouse.com website.

translations.attributionText: Rachid Maach, provided by QuranEnc. Translation and footnotes are unmodified.
translations.footnotes: [1] Le « figuier et l’olivier » désignent, selon Ibn Kathîr, Jérusalem, ville où Jésus a prêché l’Evangile. Rappelons qu’une colline bien connue porte dans cette ville le nom de « mont des Oliviers ». Le « mont Sinaï » est le lieu où le Seigneur s’est adressé à Moïse. Quant à la « cité sûre », il s’agit de la Mecque, ville natale de Mouhammad où une partie du Coran - dont justement cette sourate - a été révélée. Le Seigneur jure donc ici par trois lieux hautement symboliques pour les trois religions révélées, lieux où s’est glorieusement manifestée Sa révélation.
translations.text: Par cette cité sûre[1] !
translations.transcriptInfo: Translated by Rashid Ma’ash

tafsirEntries.providerText: 1. Allah takes an oath on the beginning of the day.
tafsirEntries.text: 1. Allah takes an oath on the beginning of the day.

translations.attributionText: Rowwad Translation Center, provided by QuranEnc. Translation and footnotes are unmodified.
translations.text: By the morning sunlight,
translations.transcriptInfo: Translated by the team of the Rowwad Translation Center, in cooperation with the Rabwah Dawah Association, the Islamic Content Service Association in Languages, and the IslamHouse.com website.

translations.attributionText: Rachid Maach, provided by QuranEnc. Translation and footnotes are unmodified.
translations.text: Par le jour qui répand sa clarté !
translations.transcriptInfo: Translated by Rashid Ma’ash

tafsirEntries.providerText: 2. And He takes an oath on the night when it darkens and people cease to move in it.
tafsirEntries.text: 2. And He takes an oath on the night when it darkens and people cease to move in it.

translations.attributionText: Rowwad Translation Center, provided by QuranEnc. Translation and footnotes are unmodified.
translations.footnotes: [1] And everything becomes still.
translations.text: and by the night when it covers with darkness[1],
translations.transcriptInfo: Translated by the team of the Rowwad Translation Center, in cooperation with the Rabwah Dawah Association, the Islamic Content Service Association in Languages, and the IslamHouse.com website.

translations.attributionText: Rachid Maach, provided by QuranEnc. Translation and footnotes are unmodified.
translations.text: Par la nuit qui étend son obscurité !
translations.transcriptInfo: Translated by Rashid Ma’ash

tafsirEntries.providerText: 3. O Messenger! Your Lord has not left you, nor has he begun to hate you, as the idolaters claimed when there was a break in the revelation.
tafsirEntries.text: 3. O Messenger! Your Lord has not left you, nor has he begun to hate you, as the idolaters claimed when there was a break in the revelation.

translations.attributionText: Rowwad Translation Center, provided by QuranEnc. Translation and footnotes are unmodified.
translations.text: your Lord has neither forsaken you [O Prophet] nor hated you;
translations.transcriptInfo: Translated by the team of the Rowwad Translation Center, in cooperation with the Rabwah Dawah Association, the Islamic Content Service Association in Languages, and the IslamHouse.com website.

translations.attributionText: Rachid Maach, provided by QuranEnc. Translation and footnotes are unmodified.
translations.text: Ton Seigneur ne t’a ni abandonné, ni détesté.
translations.transcriptInfo: Translated by Rashid Ma’ash

tafsirEntries.providerText: 4. Indeed, the abode of the afterlife is better for you than the worldly one, because of the everlasting bounties that it has.
tafsirEntries.text: 4. Indeed, the abode of the afterlife is better for you than the worldly one, because of the everlasting bounties that it has.

translations.attributionText: Rowwad Translation Center, provided by QuranEnc. Translation and footnotes are unmodified.
translations.text: the Hereafter is better for you than the present life;
translations.transcriptInfo: Translated by the team of the Rowwad Translation Center, in cooperation with the Rabwah Dawah Association, the Islamic Content Service Association in Languages, and the IslamHouse.com website.

translations.attributionText: Rachid Maach, provided by QuranEnc. Translation and footnotes are unmodified.
translations.text: L’au-delà te réserve une plus grande félicité.
translations.transcriptInfo: Translated by Rashid Ma’ash

tafsirEntries.providerText: 5. Very soon He will grant you an abundant reward, and your nation also, until you become content with what He has granted you and your nation.
tafsirEntries.text: 5. Very soon He will grant you an abundant reward, and your nation also, until you become content with what He has granted you and your nation.

translations.attributionText: Rowwad Translation Center, provided by QuranEnc. Translation and footnotes are unmodified.
translations.text: and your Lord will certainly give you so much that you will be well pleased.
translations.transcriptInfo: Translated by the team of the Rowwad Translation Center, in cooperation with the Rabwah Dawah Association, the Islamic Content Service Association in Languages, and the IslamHouse.com website.

translations.attributionText: Rachid Maach, provided by QuranEnc. Translation and footnotes are unmodified.
translations.text: Ton Seigneur t’accordera de quoi te combler.
translations.transcriptInfo: Translated by Rashid Ma’ash

tafsirEntries.providerText: 6. Verily, He found you at a time when you were a child whose father had passed away, and so He made a place of refuge for you by causing your grandfather Abdul Muttalib to become fond of you, and then your uncle Abu Talib.
tafsirEntries.text: 6. Verily, He found you at a time when you were a child whose father had passed away, and so He made a place of refuge for you by causing your grandfather Abdul Muttalib to become fond of you, and then your uncle Abu Talib.

translations.attributionText: Rowwad Translation Center, provided by QuranEnc. Translation and footnotes are unmodified.
translations.text: Did He not find you an orphan then take good care of you?
translations.transcriptInfo: Translated by the team of the Rowwad Translation Center, in cooperation with the Rabwah Dawah Association, the Islamic Content Service Association in Languages, and the IslamHouse.com website.

translations.attributionText: Rachid Maach, provided by QuranEnc. Translation and footnotes are unmodified.
translations.text: Ne t’a-t-Il pas, te trouvant orphelin, entouré d’attentions ?
translations.transcriptInfo: Translated by Rashid Ma’ash

tafsirEntries.providerText: 7. He found you in a state where you did not know what revelation or faith was, and so He taught you about that which you did not know.
tafsirEntries.text: 7. He found you in a state where you did not know what revelation or faith was, and so He taught you about that which you did not know.

translations.attributionText: Rowwad Translation Center, provided by QuranEnc. Translation and footnotes are unmodified.
translations.text: Did He not find you unguided then guide you?
translations.transcriptInfo: Translated by the team of the Rowwad Translation Center, in cooperation with the Rabwah Dawah Association, the Islamic Content Service Association in Languages, and the IslamHouse.com website.

translations.attributionText: Rachid Maach, provided by QuranEnc. Translation and footnotes are unmodified.
translations.text: Ne t’a-t-Il pas, te trouvant ignorant, enseigné la vraie foi ?
translations.transcriptInfo: Translated by Rashid Ma’ash

tafsirEntries.providerText: 8. And He found you poor, so He made you self-sufficient.
tafsirEntries.text: 8. And He found you poor, so He made you self-sufficient.

translations.attributionText: Rowwad Translation Center, provided by QuranEnc. Translation and footnotes are unmodified.
translations.text: Did He not find you in need then enrich you?
translations.transcriptInfo: Translated by the team of the Rowwad Translation Center, in cooperation with the Rabwah Dawah Association, the Islamic Content Service Association in Languages, and the IslamHouse.com website.

translations.attributionText: Rachid Maach, provided by QuranEnc. Translation and footnotes are unmodified.
translations.text: Ne t’a-t-Il pas, te trouvant démuni, placé au-dessus du besoin ?
translations.transcriptInfo: Translated by Rashid Ma’ash

tafsirEntries.providerText: 9. Therefore, do not treat badly the one who has lost his father in childhood, nor look down upon him.
tafsirEntries.text: 9. Therefore, do not treat badly the one who has lost his father in childhood, nor look down upon him.

translations.attributionText: Rowwad Translation Center, provided by QuranEnc. Translation and footnotes are unmodified.
translations.text: So do not mistreat the orphan,
translations.transcriptInfo: Translated by the team of the Rowwad Translation Center, in cooperation with the Rabwah Dawah Association, the Islamic Content Service Association in Languages, and the IslamHouse.com website.

translations.attributionText: Rachid Maach, provided by QuranEnc. Translation and footnotes are unmodified.
translations.text: Prends donc garde de traiter durement l’orphelin
translations.transcriptInfo: Translated by Rashid Ma’ash

tafsirEntries.providerText: 10. And do not rebuke the needy beggar.
tafsirEntries.text: 10. And do not rebuke the needy beggar.

translations.attributionText: Rowwad Translation Center, provided by QuranEnc. Translation and footnotes are unmodified.
translations.footnotes: [2] i.e., anyone in need who seeks help.
translations.text: nor repulse the beggar[2];
translations.transcriptInfo: Translated by the team of the Rowwad Translation Center, in cooperation with the Rabwah Dawah Association, the Islamic Content Service Association in Languages, and the IslamHouse.com website.

translations.attributionText: Rachid Maach, provided by QuranEnc. Translation and footnotes are unmodified.
translations.text: ou de repousser le mendiant sans nul ménagement.
translations.transcriptInfo: Translated by Rashid Ma’ash

tafsirEntries.providerText: 11. And be grateful for the favours of Allah upon you, and talk about them.
tafsirEntries.text: 11. And be grateful for the favours of Allah upon you, and talk about them.

translations.attributionText: Rowwad Translation Center, provided by QuranEnc. Translation and footnotes are unmodified.
translations.footnotes: [3] i.e., be grateful to Allah by proclaiming the favors He has given you.
translations.text: and proclaim the favors of your Lord[3].
translations.transcriptInfo: Translated by the team of the Rowwad Translation Center, in cooperation with the Rabwah Dawah Association, the Islamic Content Service Association in Languages, and the IslamHouse.com website.

translations.attributionText: Rachid Maach, provided by QuranEnc. Translation and footnotes are unmodified.
translations.text: Et proclame les grâces de ton Seigneur hautement !
translations.transcriptInfo: Translated by Rashid Ma’ash

tafsirEntries.providerText: 1. Verily, Allah has opened up your heart for you and made receiving revelation beloved to you.
tafsirEntries.text: 1. Verily, Allah has opened up your heart for you and made receiving revelation beloved to you.

translations.attributionText: Rowwad Translation Center, provided by QuranEnc. Translation and footnotes are unmodified.
translations.footnotes: [1] i.e., enlighten and gladden your heart for receiving the revelation.
translations.text: Have We not reassured your heart for you [O Prophet][1],
translations.transcriptInfo: Translated by the team of the Rowwad Translation Center, in cooperation with the Rabwah Dawah Association, the Islamic Content Service Association in Languages, and the IslamHouse.com website.

translations.attributionText: Rachid Maach, provided by QuranEnc. Translation and footnotes are unmodified.
translations.text: N’avons-Nous pas épanoui ton cœur,
translations.transcriptInfo: Translated by Rashid Ma’ash

tafsirEntries.providerText: 2. And I have removed sin from you.
tafsirEntries.text: 2. And I have removed sin from you.

translations.attributionText: Rowwad Translation Center, provided by QuranEnc. Translation and footnotes are unmodified.
translations.footnotes: [2] forgave your previous or future errors, or relieved you of the anxiety you experienced at the beginning of your mission.
translations.text: and relieved you of your burden[2]
translations.transcriptInfo: Translated by the team of the Rowwad Translation Center, in cooperation with the Rabwah Dawah Association, the Islamic Content Service Association in Languages, and the IslamHouse.com website.

translations.attributionText: Rachid Maach, provided by QuranEnc. Translation and footnotes are unmodified.
translations.text: te soulageant ainsi de ce fardeau
translations.transcriptInfo: Translated by Rashid Ma’ash

tafsirEntries.providerText: 3. That which was burdening you to the extent that it almost broke your back.
tafsirEntries.text: 3. That which was burdening you to the extent that it almost broke your back.

translations.attributionText: Rowwad Translation Center, provided by QuranEnc. Translation and footnotes are unmodified.
translations.text: that weighed down your back,
translations.transcriptInfo: Translated by the team of the Rowwad Translation Center, in cooperation with the Rabwah Dawah Association, the Islamic Content Service Association in Languages, and the IslamHouse.com website.

translations.attributionText: Rachid Maach, provided by QuranEnc. Translation and footnotes are unmodified.
translations.text: qui pesait si lourdement sur ton dos ?
translations.transcriptInfo: Translated by Rashid Ma’ash

tafsirEntries.providerText: 4. And I elevated for you your mention, so you are now remembered in the call to prayer, and the call preceding the prayer, and at other times.
tafsirEntries.text: 4. And I elevated for you your mention, so you are now remembered in the call to prayer, and the call preceding the prayer, and at other times.

translations.attributionText: Rowwad Translation Center, provided by QuranEnc. Translation and footnotes are unmodified.
translations.footnotes: [3] Allah raised the Prophet's name in numerous ways, such as his name is mentioned twice in the call to prayer five times a day, as well the second call to prayer; at the end of each of the five daily prayers; believers invoke Allah’s blessings upon him and his family; and upon reverting to Islam, his name is mentioned, etc.
translations.text: and raised high your fame for you[3]?
translations.transcriptInfo: Translated by the team of the Rowwad Translation Center, in cooperation with the Rabwah Dawah Association, the Islamic Content Service Association in Languages, and the IslamHouse.com website.

translations.attributionText: Rachid Maach, provided by QuranEnc. Translation and footnotes are unmodified.
translations.text: N’avons-Nous pas rehaussé ton renom ?
translations.transcriptInfo: Translated by Rashid Ma’ash

tafsirEntries.providerText: 5. Indeed, with difficulty and constraint, comes ease and options.
tafsirEntries.text: 5. Indeed, with difficulty and constraint, comes ease and options.

translations.attributionText: Rowwad Translation Center, provided by QuranEnc. Translation and footnotes are unmodified.
translations.footnotes: [4] In Arabic grammar, if a definite noun is repeated, it is referring to the same thing. However, if an indefinite noun is repeated, it is referring to two different things. So here in this and the coming verse they refer to one hardship (a definite noun) and two eases (an indefinite noun), which manifests Allah's favors upon His servants even in times of hardships.
translations.text: For indeed, with hardship comes ease[4],
translations.transcriptInfo: Translated by the team of the Rowwad Translation Center, in cooperation with the Rabwah Dawah Association, the Islamic Content Service Association in Languages, and the IslamHouse.com website.

translations.attributionText: Rachid Maach, provided by QuranEnc. Translation and footnotes are unmodified.
translations.text: Sache qu’il n’est d’épreuve qui ne soit suivie d’une délivrance.
translations.transcriptInfo: Translated by Rashid Ma’ash

tafsirEntries.providerText: 6. Indeed, with difficulty and constraint, comes ease and options; when you know that well, the troubling of your people will not terrify you and will not stop you from calling towards Allah.
tafsirEntries.text: 6. Indeed, with difficulty and constraint, comes ease and options; when you know that well, the troubling of your people will not terrify you and will not stop you from calling towards Allah.

translations.attributionText: Rowwad Translation Center, provided by QuranEnc. Translation and footnotes are unmodified.
translations.text: indeed, with hardship comes ease.
translations.transcriptInfo: Translated by the team of the Rowwad Translation Center, in cooperation with the Rabwah Dawah Association, the Islamic Content Service Association in Languages, and the IslamHouse.com website.

translations.attributionText: Rachid Maach, provided by QuranEnc. Translation and footnotes are unmodified.
translations.text: Oui, il n’est pas d’épreuve qui ne soit suivie d’une délivrance.
translations.transcriptInfo: Translated by Rashid Ma’ash

tafsirEntries.providerText: 7. So when you finish your work and complete it, strive in the worship of your Lord.
tafsirEntries.text: 7. So when you finish your work and complete it, strive in the worship of your Lord.

translations.attributionText: Rowwad Translation Center, provided by QuranEnc. Translation and footnotes are unmodified.

Rappelons qu’une colline bien connue porte dans cette ville le nom de « mont des Oliviers ». Le « mont Sinaï » est le lieu où le Seigneur s’est adressé à Moïse. Quant à la « cité sûre », il s’agit de la Mecque, ville natale de Mouhammad où une partie du Coran - dont justement cette sourate - a été révélée. translationSegments.text: By the morning sunlight,
and by the night when it covers with darkness[1],
your Lord has neither forsaken you [O Prophet] nor hated you;
the Hereafter is better for you than the present life;

activity.instruction: Match each ayah to its unchanged translation.

translationSegments.text: and your Lord will certainly give you so much that you will be well pleased.
Did He not find you an orphan then take good care of you?
Did He not find you unguided then guide you?
Did He not find you in need then enrich you?

activity.instruction: Match each ayah to its unchanged translation.

translationSegments.text: So do not mistreat the orphan,
nor repulse the beggar[2];
and proclaim the favors of your Lord[3].

activity.instruction: Match each ayah to its unchanged translation.

and by Mount Sinai[2],

Is not Allah the Most Just of all judges?

translationSegments.text: Read in the name of your Lord Who created,
created man from a clinging clot.
Read, and your Lord is the Most Generous,
Who taught by the pen,

activity.instruction: Match each ayah to its unchanged translation.

translationSegments.text: taught man what he did not know[1].
Indeed, man transgresses
when he deems himself to be self-sufficient.
Indeed, to your Lord is the return.

activity.instruction: Match each ayah to its unchanged translation.

translationSegments.text: Have you seen the one who prevents[2]
a slave [of Allah] from praying[3]?
What if this [slave] is rightly guided,
and enjoins righteousness?

activity.instruction: Match each ayah to its unchanged translation.

translationSegments.text: How about the one who denies and turns away[4]?
Does he not know that Allah is watching all?
No indeed; if he does not desist, We will surely drag him by the forelock[5]
a lying, sinful forelock[6].

activity.instruction: Match each ayah to its unchanged translation.

translationSegments.text: So let him call his associates;
We will call the wardens of Hellfire[7].
No indeed; do not obey him, but prostrate and draw near [to Allah].

activity.instruction: Match each ayah to its unchanged translation.

translationSegments.text: Those who disbelieve from the People of the Book and the polytheists were not going to desist [from disbelief][1] until there came to them clear proof,
a messenger from Allah, reciting pure pages[2]
containing upright commandments.
Yet those who were given the Scripture did not disagree[3] except after the clear proof came to them,

activity.instruction: Match each ayah to its unchanged translation.

translationSegments.text: although they were commanded only to worship Allah with sincere devotion to Him, being inclined to the true faith, and to establish prayer and give zakah; that is the true religion.
Those who disbelieve from the People of the Book and the polytheists will be in the fire of Hell, abiding therein forever. It is they who are the worst of creatures.
As for those who believe and do righteous deeds – it is they who are the best of creatures.
Their reward with their Lord is Gardens of Eternity under which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. Allah is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him. This is for those who fear their Lord.

activity.instruction: Match each ayah to its unchanged translation.

translationSegments.text: When the earth is shaken with a mighty quake,
and the earth throws out its burdens[1],
and man says[2], “What is the matter with it?”
On that Day it will recount all its news,

activity.instruction: Match each ayah to its unchanged translation.

translationSegments.text: because your Lord has inspired it [to do so].
On that Day all people will come forward in separate groups to be shown their deeds[3].
So whoever does an atom’s weight[4] of good will see it,
and whoever does an atom’s weight of evil will see it.

translationSegments.text: By the galloping, panting horses[1],
striking sparks of fire [with their hooves][2],
launching raids at dawn[3],
stirring up thereby clouds of dust,

activity.instruction: Match each ayah to its unchanged translation.

translationSegments.text: plunging thereby into the midst of the enemy[4],
indeed, man is very ungrateful to his Lord[5] –
and he himself is a witness to that[6] –
and he is truly extreme in his love of wealth.

activity.instruction: Match each ayah to its unchanged translation.

translationSegments.text: Does he not know that when the contents of graves will be overturned,
and the secrets of the hearts will be brought to light[7]?
Indeed, their Lord is All-Aware of them on that Day[8].

translationSegments.text: The Striking Calamity!
What is the Striking Calamity?
How do you know what the Striking Calamity is?
On that Day people will be like scattered moths[1],

activity.instruction: Match each ayah to its unchanged translation.

translationSegments.text: and the mountains will be like carded wool[2].
Then the one whose scales of good deeds are heavy,
will have a pleasant life[3].
But the one whose scales of good deeds are light,

activity.instruction: Match each ayah to its unchanged translation.

translationSegments.text: his abode will be the abyss[4].
And how do you know what it is?
It is a Blazing Fire.

activity.instruction: Match each ayah to its unchanged translation.

translations.footnotes: [3] This passage refers to the land of the three great prophets of Allah: Jesus (ﷺ) lived in the land of figs and olives, Moses (ﷺ) communicated with Allah on Mount Sinai, and Muhammad's (ﷺ) birthplace was Makkah. There is a similar reference in Deuteronomy 33:1, [Moses said:] “The Lord came from Sinai. Rising from Seir upon us, and he shone forth from Mount Paran.” Seir is a mountain near Jerusalem, and Paran is a mountain near Makkah.

Rappelons qu’une colline bien connue porte dans cette ville le nom de « mont des Oliviers ». Le « mont Sinaï » est le lieu où le Seigneur s’est adressé à Moïse. Quant à la « cité sûre », il s’agit de la Mecque, ville natale de Mouhammad où une partie du Coran - dont justement cette sourate - a été révélée. Le Seigneur jure donc ici par trois lieux hautement symboliques pour les trois religions révélées, lieux où s’est glorieusement manifestée Sa révélation.

translationSegments.text: Par le jour qui répand sa clarté !
Par la nuit qui étend son obscurité !
Ton Seigneur ne t’a ni abandonné, ni détesté.
L’au-delà te réserve une plus grande félicité.

activity.instruction: Associez chaque verset à sa traduction inchangée.

translationSegments.text: Ton Seigneur t’accordera de quoi te combler.
Ne t’a-t-Il pas, te trouvant orphelin, entouré d’attentions ?
Ne t’a-t-Il pas, te trouvant ignorant, enseigné la vraie foi ?
Ne t’a-t-Il pas, te trouvant démuni, placé au-dessus du besoin ?

activity.instruction: Associez chaque verset à sa traduction inchangée.

translationSegments.text: Prends donc garde de traiter durement l’orphelin
ou de repousser le mendiant sans nul ménagement.
Et proclame les grâces de ton Seigneur hautement !

activity.instruction: Associez chaque verset à sa traduction inchangée.

translationSegments.text: N’avons-Nous pas épanoui ton cœur,
te soulageant ainsi de ce fardeau
qui pesait si lourdement sur ton dos ?
N’avons-Nous pas rehaussé ton renom ?

activity.instruction: Associez chaque verset à sa traduction inchangée.

translationSegments.text: Sache qu’il n’est d’épreuve qui ne soit suivie d’une délivrance.
Oui, il n’est pas d’épreuve qui ne soit suivie d’une délivrance.
Une fois donc libéré de tes occupations, consacre-toi au culte avec ferveur,
te tournant sincèrement vers ton Seigneur, convoitant humblement Ses faveurs.

translationSegments.text: Par le figuier et l’olivier !
Par le mont Sinaï !
Par cette cité sûre[1] !
Nous avons créé l’homme en le dotant de la nature la plus pure[2],

activity.instruction: Associez chaque verset à sa traduction inchangée.

translationSegments.text: avant de lui faire connaître la plus infâme déchéance[3].
A l’exception de ceux qui croient et accomplissent de bonnes œuvres, auxquels est réservée une récompense dont ils ne seront jamais privés.
Qu’est-ce qui peut, après cela, vous faire encore douter du Jugement dernier ?
Allah n’est-Il pas le plus équitable et le plus sage des juges ?

activity.instruction: Associez chaque verset à sa traduction inchangée.

translationSegments.text: Lis au nom de ton Seigneur qui a créé,
qui a créé l’homme d’un corps accroché[1].
Lis ! Ton Seigneur est toute bonté,
Lui qui, par le calame, a enseigné[2],

activity.instruction: Associez chaque verset à sa traduction inchangée.

translationSegments.text: apprenant à l’homme ce qu’il ignorait.
Mais en vérité l’homme se montre hautain
dès qu’il se croit au-dessus du besoin,
oubliant qu’il fera retour à ton Seigneur.

activity.instruction: Associez chaque verset à sa traduction inchangée.

translationSegments.text: N’as-tu pas vu cet impie qui prétend interdire
à un serviteur d’Allah d’accomplir la prière,
alors qu’il se contente de suivre le droit chemin
et d’inciter les hommes à craindre Allah,

activity.instruction: Associez chaque verset à sa traduction inchangée.

translationSegments.text: tandis que cet impie renie la vérité et se détourne de la foi ?
Ne sait-il donc pas qu’Allah le voit ?
S’il ne cesse pas, Nous le traînerons par le toupet[3],
le toupet d’un menteur et d’un pécheur invétéré.

activity.instruction: Associez chaque verset à sa traduction inchangée.

translationSegments.text: Qu’il fasse alors appel à tous ses partisans.
Nous ferons appel aux anges du châtiment.
Ne l’écoute pas ! Mais, par la prière, rapproche-toi[4] !

activity.instruction: Associez chaque verset à sa traduction inchangée.

translationSegments.text: Nous l’avons révélé[1] au cours de la Nuit des décrets divins[2].
Mais qui pourrait t’indiquer ce qu’est la Nuit des décrets divins ?
La Nuit des décrets divins est plus bénie que mille mois réunis[3].
Porteurs de tous les arrêts divins[4], les anges et l’Esprit[5] descendent sur ordre de leur Seigneur au cours de cette nuit.

activity.instruction: Associez chaque verset à sa traduction inchangée.

translationSegments.text: C’est une nuit remplie de paix et de bénédiction jusqu’à l’apparition de l’aube.

translationSegments.text: Les mécréants, parmi les gens du Livre et les idolâtres, ne pouvaient[1] renoncer à leurs croyances avant d’avoir reçu une preuve d’une grande clarté :
l’avènement d’un Messager envoyé par Allah leur récitant des feuillets d’une grande pureté,
renfermant des enseignements d’une parfaite justice, d’une infinie sagesse et d’une indéniable authenticité[2].
Or, ceux qui ont reçu les Ecritures ne se sont divisés qu’après avoir reçu une preuve d’une grande clarté,

activity.instruction: Associez chaque verset à sa traduction inchangée.

translationSegments.text: un livre leur ordonnant simplement d’adorer Allah en Lui vouant un culte exclusif et sincère, d’accomplir la prière et de faire la charité, professant ainsi la religion de vérité.
Les mécréants, parmi les gens du Livre et les idolâtres, sont donc voués au feu de la Géhenne où ils demeureront pour l’éternité. Voilà les êtres les plus abjects de l’humanité.
Quant à ceux qui croient et accomplissent de bonnes œuvres, ce sont les êtres les plus nobles de l’humanité.

En récompense de leur foi, ils seront admis auprès de leur Seigneur dans les jardins d’Eden traversés de rivières, entièrement satisfaits d’Allah qui sera Lui-même satisfait d’eux. Voilà comment ceux qui craignent leur Seigneur seront récompensés pour l’éternité.

activity.instruction: Associez chaque verset à sa traduction inchangée.

translationSegments.text: Le Grand choc !
Qu’est-ce que le Grand choc ?
Qui pourrait t’indiquer ce qu’est le Grand choc ?
Ce Jour-là, les hommes s’éparpilleront comme des papillons[1],

activity.instruction: Associez chaque verset à sa traduction inchangée.

translationSegments.text: et les montagnes auront, des flocons de laine cardée, la légèreté.

Quant à celui dont la balance penchera du mauvais côté,

activity.instruction: Associez chaque verset à sa traduction inchangée.

translationSegments.text: il sera, dans l’Abîme, violemment précipité.
Mais qui pourrait te décrire sa réalité ?
Un feu ardent à jamais attisé !

translationSegments.text: Dis : « Allah est la seule et unique divinité.
Allah est le Maître dont nul ne peut se passer[1].
Il n’a pas engendré, ni été Lui-même engendré.
Et nul dans Sa création n’est à même de L’égaler. »

contre le mal de la nuit qui étend son obscurité,
contre le charme maléfique de tous les sorciers[1],
